sources.entry: OpenEmu - Retro video game emulation for macOS.

summary.one_liner: OpenEmu is an open-source macOS application for retro video game emulation that loads multiple emulation engines as plugins behind a native macOS front end.
summary.what_it_does: OpenEmu is a macOS game emulator front end built on Cocoa, Metal, and Core Animation, with Sparkle used for auto-updating. Its modular architecture lets game-engine plugins supply the emulation, so one interface can run many systems. The README lists supported systems and their engines, including Atari 2600 (Stella), Game Boy/Color (Gambatte), Game Boy Advance (mGBA), GameCube (Dolphin), Nintendo DS (DeSmuME), N64 (Mupen64Plus), SNES (BSNES, Snes9x), Sega Genesis (Genesis Plus), PlayStation (Mednafen), and PSP (PPSSPP). The README does not describe usage details beyond the engine list and build requirements.
use_cases: play retro console games on a Mac
emulate Nintendo, Sega, Atari, and Sony systems on macOS
run multiple emulator cores in one app
build an emulator for macOS from source
notable: Modular plugin architecture where each emulation engine is a separate plugin
Supports dozens of consoles via engines such as Stella, Mednafen, Genesis Plus, and Dolphin
Native macOS front end rather than a cross-platform UI
caveats: Building the default branch requires Xcode 14.3 and macOS Ventura
keywords: play old console games on mac
